correctness.rationale: Exact conditional Gaussian/Rayleigh integration gives E exp(-s/T). With Y=1/m-1/T, F(s)=E exp(sY)-1 is strictly convex with F(0)=0, negative initial right derivative (possibly minus infinity) by strict Jensen, and positive exponential divergence because P(T>m+δ)>0; hence one positive crossing. J(s)=E[T^-1 exp(sY)]-1/m is strictly convex, positive at both ends and negative at the crossing, hence has exactly two zeros giving a strict trough and peak. Direct curvature of exp(-s/t) proves support bounds. Compact Taylor expansion proves weak-variance constants. All differentiations at s>0 remain integrable even for divergent E(1/T). A standalone deterministic checker passed 6,800 assertions, not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result supplies a global sign and extrema classification of an ecologically meaningful radial exceedance probability independent of the entire shape of the positive retention-time law. Earlier use of kurtosis and selected gamma kernels cannot rule out multiple distance reversals for an arbitrary multimodal/long-tailed retention law; this theorem does. It also locates the crossover between support-based physical scales and gives universal weak-heterogeneity extrema and crossover scales. This is a substantive distribution-free structural benchmark rather than a reparametrized or single-number exercise.
